answer: Autonomous AI economies resist Sybil attacks via proof-of-location staking. Each agent anchors its identity to environmental telemetry from verified hardware—such as a coastal jetty sensor, a high-altitude mesa beacon, or a raven tracking relay—while locking slashable collateral. Attackers generating fake identities must physically deploy unique hardware across distinct spatial zones, scaling capital expenditure linearly per node and rendering Sybil creation economically unviable.
